anomalies.observed: The POT net joins the potentiometer connector's wiper (J3.2), the MCU ADC-capable pins (U2.2 and U3.2), the P-MOSFET drain (Q1.3), and fan connector pin J2.2. Q1 can therefore drive the same node used as the potentiometer input.
anomalies.expected: The potentiometer wiper/MCU input should be separate from the switched fan output, or an explicit circuit should isolate and appropriately sense the two. The connector wiring indicates J3 is a potentiometer connection: its outer pins are on +5V and GND, while its middle pin is on POT.

evidence.quote: POT : J2.2(Pin_2,passive) J3.2(Pin_2,passive) ... Q1.3(D,passive) U2.2(XTAL1/PB3,bidirectional) U3.2(PB3,bidirectional)

anomalies.impact: When Q1 switches the fan output, it also drives the potentiometer wiper and MCU input, overriding the knob's setting and potentially sending fan-output transients or current into the control-input circuit.

anomalies.observed: Both the ATtiny45 (U2) and ATtiny13 (U3) are connected to the same SDA, PWM, and SCK nets; their power, ground, reset, POT, and TACH connections are also shared.
anomalies.expected: Only one MCU should drive these shared signals at a time, or the design should provide explicit selection/isolation if both MCU footprints are alternatives.

evidence.quote: PWM : J4.1(MISO,passive) R2.1(passive) R5.2(passive) U2.6(PB1,bidirectional) U3.6(PB1,bidirectional)

anomalies.impact: If both ICs are populated, their GPIOs are directly connected and can contend when they drive different logic levels, making control and programming unreliable. This may be intended as an unpopulated-alternative footprint arrangement, but no selection or assembly note is present in the supplied files.

parsed.summary: The POT net combines the potentiometer wiper and MCU input with the switched fan-output node, so switching the fan can override the control input. The netlist also connects two different MCU devices in parallel on shared GPIOs, which risks contention if both are populated.
